discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of single microwave photons to superconducting artificial atoms
subfield: Condensed matter / quantum optics with superconducting circuits
motivation: The 2025 prize recognised that electrical circuits can behave as macroscopic quantum objects. The next conceptual step was to let such circuits talk to single photons. In 2004 Blais and co-workers proposed, and Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues demonstrated, the strong coupling of a superconducting qubit to a single microwave photon in an on-chip resonator. This created circuit quantum electrodynamics, bringing the physics of cavity QED onto a chip with coupling strengths far exceeding those in atomic systems. Circuit QED opened new regimes of light-matter interaction, including photon-number resolution, microwave Fock and cat states, and ultrastrong coupling. It also provided dispersive qubit readout, bus-mediated two-qubit gates and quantum error correction. Today it is the architecture of essentially every superconducting quantum processor worldwide and a platform for hybrid quantum systems with spins, magnons and mechanics. It is a clean, reproducible discovery that founded a field and a technology.
